Lessons.Title: Solving Systems with Inverses
ExplanationParagraphs: A square matrix A is invertible only if determinant is nonzero.
For nonsingular system AX=b, solution X=A^-1b.
Use Gauss-Jordan on [A|I] to compute A^-1.
A zero row/column causes singularity, but zero diagonal alone does not.
Inverse method applies to two- and three-unknown financial systems.
Independent Cool-down: demonstrate a valid example of the section's central operation and check exact answer.
